reading.title: How Writers Keep You Turning Pages
reading.purpose: Discover the story craft tools authors use to build characters, tension, and endings.
paras: Have you ever read a book you could not put down? Writers use smart tools to make a tale feel real from page one to the end.

Each tale starts with a narrator, the voice that tells the events. Through small acts, the writer shows each trait, like kindness or grit. We also see a hero's attitude, the way they think and feel about hard jobs. When trouble hits, we watch their reaction to see what they do next.

At the heart of a plot sits a conflict, a big problem the hero must face. Fixing it takes a real struggle, a hard fight with bumps along the way. At times the writer adds a flashback, a scene that steps back in time to show why a hero feels scared or bold.

To build suspense, that tense wish to know what comes next, writers drop small clues instead of telling all at once. Near the end, they disclose the hidden truth. Then comes the resolution, the point when the main problem is solved.
Once you spot these tools, you can see how each scene fits.

choices: the final scene when the main problem is solved
a scene that goes back to an earlier time
the voice of the person telling the whole story
a secret clue hidden in the very last chapter
qs.why: Paragraph 3 defines a flashback as "a scene that steps back to an earlier time."

qs.q: Which sentence defines the narrator of a story?
choices: Each tale starts with a narrator, the voice that tells the events.
When trouble hits, we watch their reaction to see what they do next.
At the heart of a plot sits a conflict, a big problem the hero must face.
Once you spot these tools, you can see how each scene fits.
qs.why: This sentence explains that the narrator is the voice that tells the events.

ev.text: Each tale starts with a narrator, the voice that tells the events.

qs.q: Why do writers drop small clues instead of telling a secret right away?
choices: To build suspense so readers feel eager to find out what happens.
Because the narrator usually forgets the resolution until the final chapter.
To make the character's attitude seem unfriendly toward every other person.
Because flashbacks are never allowed to appear near the start of a book.
qs.why: Paragraph 4 says writers drop small clues instead of telling everything at once in order to build suspense.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Every good book must hide a secret until the very last sentence of the story.
Authors use specific craft tools to make characters, plots, and endings engaging.
A character's reaction to trouble is much more important than the story's ending.
Flashbacks are the only way an author can explain why a character feels brave.
qs.why: The reading explains how tools like narrator, conflict, flashback, suspense, and resolution work together in a story.
